The relevant excerpts: DOC-010 part 1: SSO sign-in option only appears for email domain configured and only once identity provider sync has created the account. Also DOC-010 part 3: admin can check whether the account exists from Settings → People, where an SSO-provisioned account is marked with identity provider; its absence means sync hasn't created it yet.

Thus we can answer: The SSO button appears only if your domain is set up for SSO and your account has been provisioned via the IdP sync. Ask admin to verify account exists in Settings → People; if not, sync hasn't run yet. Also ensure domain is configured. Provide steps.

2. The sync hasn’t created your account – an admin can verify this in **Settings → People**; an SSO‑provisioned account will be listed with the identity provider shown next to it. If it’s missing, the sync hasn’t run or your account wasn’t provisioned.

arguments.message:
The SSO sign‑in button only shows up for staff whose email domain is configured for SSO **and** whose account has already been created by the identity‑provider sync. If you don’t see the button, it usually means one of two things:

1. Your workspace hasn’t added your email domain to the SSO configuration yet.
2. The sync hasn’t created your account – an admin can verify this in **Settings → People**; an SSO‑provisioned account will be listed with the identity provider shown next to it. If it’s missing, the sync hasn’t run or your account wasn’t provisioned.

Ask your admin to check the domain settings and confirm that your account appears in the People list. Once the account is provisioned, the SSO button will appear on the sign‑in screen.
